definitions.explanation: A mammal that lives primarily in the ocean, such as seals, sea lions, walruses, and sea otters. A zoological term.

examples.japanese: {水族館|すいぞくかん}で{海獣|かいじゅう}のショーを{見|み}た。
examples.english: I watched a marine mammal show at the aquarium.

examples.japanese: アザラシやセイウチは{海獣|かいじゅう}に{分類|ぶんるい}される。
examples.english: Seals and walruses are classified as marine mammals.

examples.japanese: {北海道|ほっかいどう}の{海岸|かいがん}では{野生|やせい}の{海獣|かいじゅう}を{観察|かんさつ}できることがある。
examples.english: On the coasts of Hokkaido, it is sometimes possible to observe wild marine mammals.

notes: Composed of {海|かい} (sea) + {獣|じゅう} (beast, animal). Refers specifically to marine mammals — not fish or other sea creatures. Includes animals like アザラシ (seal), アシカ (sea lion), セイウチ (walrus), ラッコ (sea otter), and sometimes クジラ (whale) and イルカ (dolphin). Not to be confused with the homophone {怪獣|かいじゅう} (monster, as in Godzilla). Common collocations: {海獣|かいじゅう}{類|るい} (marine mammals as a group), {海獣|かいじゅう}ショー (marine mammal show). In Japanese aquariums, the {海獣|かいじゅう} section typically features pinnipeds (seals and sea lions).
